about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: the topic's target words in new sentences, never shown on its pages, Boards or in Defuse.

rounds.prompt: When I asked him where Ana was, he just ___ — he had no idea.
rounds.note: shrug = lift your shoulders to show you don't know.

rounds.prompt: Stop ___ in your seat and sit still!
rounds.note: fidget = keep moving because you're bored or nervous.

rounds.prompt: Exhausted, she ___ onto the sofa and closed her eyes.
rounds.note: slump = sit or fall down heavily.

rounds.prompt: He ___ his eyes and yawned.
rounds.note: rub your eyes when you're tired.

rounds.prompt: She took a quick ___ at her watch.
rounds.note: a glance = a quick look.

rounds.prompt: The angry driver gave me a furious ___.
rounds.note: a glare = an angry look.

rounds.prompt: He gave me a ___ to show he was only joking.
rounds.note: a wink = closing one eye quickly as a signal.

rounds.prompt: My parents are very ___ — they let me do almost anything.
rounds.note: easy-going = relaxed, not strict.

rounds.prompt: Be ___ when you cross this road — cars come round the corner fast.
rounds.note: cautious = careful to avoid danger.

rounds.prompt: It was ___ of him to tell her she looked tired.
rounds.note: tactless = saying things that upset people.

rounds.prompt: He's so ___ — he thinks he's better than everyone else.
rounds.note: arrogant = thinking you are better than others.

rounds.prompt: 'Don't wake the baby,' she ___.
rounds.note: whisper = speak very quietly.

rounds.prompt: He was so nervous that he ___ his way through the speech.
rounds.note: stammer = speak with pauses and repeated sounds.

rounds.prompt: We ___ for hours about our holiday plans.
rounds.note: chat = talk in a friendly, informal way.

rounds.prompt: She ___ for a moment before answering the question.
rounds.note: hesitate = pause before doing something.

rounds.prompt: She wears her watch on her left ___.
rounds.note: the wrist joins your hand to your arm.

rounds.prompt: I've got a sore ___ — it hurts when I swallow.
rounds.note: a sore throat.

rounds.prompt: After months without rain, the ___ destroyed the farmers' crops.
rounds.note: a drought = a long time without rain.

rounds.prompt: There was a ___ last night, so we ate dinner by candlelight.
rounds.note: a blackout = the electricity goes off.

rounds.prompt: Skiers were warned about the risk of an ___ after the heavy snow.
rounds.note: an avalanche = snow falling down a mountain.

rounds.prompt: Don't be so ___ — leave some cake for the others!
rounds.note: greedy = wanting more than your share.

rounds.prompt: My sister is really ___ — happy one minute, angry the next.
rounds.note: moody = changing mood quickly.

rounds.prompt: I'm so ___ — I've broken another glass!
rounds.note: clumsy = often dropping or breaking things.

rounds.prompt: Stop being so ___ and telling everyone what to do!
rounds.note: bossy = always telling people what to do.

rounds.prompt: A ___ broke into our house while we were on holiday.
rounds.note: a burglar = someone who breaks into buildings to steal.

rounds.prompt: A ___ took my phone on the crowded bus without me noticing.
rounds.note: a pickpocket = steals from pockets and bags.

rounds.prompt: Her video went ___ and got two million views in a day.
rounds.note: go viral = spread fast online.

rounds.prompt: The road was closed, so we had to make a ___.
rounds.note: a detour = a longer way round.

rounds.prompt: Keep your ___ in case you need to return the shoes.
rounds.note: a receipt = proof that you paid.

rounds.prompt: I need to finish this essay tonight — the ___ is tomorrow morning.
rounds.note: a deadline = the time something must be done by.

rounds.prompt: The ___ gave the film only two stars in her review.
rounds.note: a critic = someone who reviews films, books or art.
